items.title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
items.summary: smolmaxxing is a patch for llama.cpp that enables 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models to run on devices with approximately 1 GB of RAM by using custom kernels and streaming weights from flash storage. Measured results show a 16B model running at 5.1 tok/s on a Xiaomi TV Box S and 2.6-4.5 tok/s on an iPad Air (2013).
items.why_it_matters: The techniques allow large language models to operate on legacy hardware like TV boxes and old tablets by keeping only part of the model in memory and reading the rest from flash as needed.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and follow the README to benchmark on your target device.

items.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled GPUs
items.summary: Forensic analysis of model weights reveals that six AI models released by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group since April 2026 contain numerical patterns matching NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, indicating the hardware was used to initialize these models. The evidence, derived from published weights rather than leaks, suggests these developers accessed export-controlled chips despite restrictions, with the strongest statistical matches reaching up to 1,385 sigma.
items.why_it_matters: The findings provide technical evidence that leading Chinese AI developers have accessed advanced computing hardware restricted from export to China, although they do not establish how access was obtained or whether export controls were violated.
items.next_step_detail: Read the full forensic report and audit any Blackwell‑trained models in your stack.

items.title: Turning a 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive into RCE
items.summary: A 22-year-old zero-day in PostgreSQL core involves a new class of type-confusion vulnerabilities where changing a composite type field leads to memory corruption. The discovery originated from exploiting the pg_clickhouse extension and investigating how PostgreSQL represents data types via OIDs.
items.why_it_matters: The vulnerability allows for reliable memory corruption by manipulating how PostgreSQL interprets Datum values, exposing core database internals to potential exploitation.
items.next_step_detail: Upgrade PostgreSQL to the version that includes the CVE‑2026‑6460 fix or apply the provided patch from the advisory.

items.title: Your MCP Servers Are Silently Draining Your Context Window: The Hidden Cost of Tool-Heavy AI Agents
items.summary: Attaching multiple Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers injects thousands of tokens of JSON schema definitions into every API request, which degrades reasoning accuracy and slows time-to-first-token. The entry provides a TypeScript script to audit the token footprint of these tool definitions.
items.why_it_matters: It quantifies the hidden token costs and attention dilution caused by bloated tool schemas, allowing developers to measure the impact of their MCP configurations on model performance.
items.next_step_detail: Study the micro‑tool pattern and refactor one of your existing agents accordingly.
